Subject: Redwood load test plan & SLOs — FinanceCorp

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the chat this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we all have the same picture: 

Summary of SLOs you called out:
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn text generation (avg token output)
- Throughput: sustain 250 requests/sec during peak window
- Concurrency: up to 500 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled
- Streaming: support chunked streaming (client-side) with <100ms first-byte

What Redwood will provide for the customer-led load test:
- A test account (api key scoped to test environment) and a sandbox model variant optimized for load
- Reference k6 script (attached) and a short Locust variant if you prefer
- IP allowlist file for your infra team to add our test IPs
- A brief pre-test checklist and runbook for failure modes

Proposed test window: Thu 2027-03-10, 10:00–12:00 PT — please confirm if that still works.

Action items:
1) Samantha / Rahul: confirm latency/throughput targets above or call out changes (reply by EOD Tue)
2) Redwood (Aditya): share k6 script + test API key and IP allowlist (I copied Aditya on this)
3) Logistics: Marissa will own run coordination and results capture

Thanks — happy to adjust the window if you need evenings or a different day.

—

Subject: k6 script + test credentials for FinanceCorp load run

Hi Samantha / Rahul — attaching the reference k6 script we discussed and a CSV of our test IPs. Notes below: 

- k6 script (k6-financecorp-script.js): configured to ramp to 250 RPS over 10 minutes, sustain for 60 minutes, then ramp down. Includes a streaming mode using the /v1/streams endpoint with chunk size set to 128 bytes for first-byte timing.
- Sandbox model: redwood-sandbox-v2 (CPU/GPU-mixed variant) — optimized for stable latency and has prefix caching enabled. Expect baseline p95 ~90–130ms at 250 rps depending on token length. We'll validate during the warm-up.
- Test API key: FINANCECORP-TEST-abc123 (scoped, expires 2027-03-15)
- IP allowlist (financecorp-ip-allowlist.csv): 52.23.45.120/32, 18.210.33.9/32, 34.201.12.7/32. Please add these to your firewall ahead of the run.

Runbook highlights:
1) Warm-up: 20 minutes at 50% load to populate caches
2) Load phase: ramp to 250 rps, sustain for 60 minutes. Monitor p95 latency and first-byte times.
3) Failure triggers: error rate >1% sustained for 5 minutes OR p95 > 300ms for 5 minutes
4) Rollback: we'll throttle tests and fail closed if service impact observed; notify infra and pause.

I've also posted a read-only run plan here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xFinancecorp-MAP (link shared with your @financecorp.com addresses).

Let me know if you want a Locust file instead — we can drop one in the same folder.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Can you confirm the source ports you'll use? (our firewall rules require both IP and port ranges)
- Can the test key be rate-limited to the sandbox only? We want to ensure no cross-tenant bleed.
- For streaming first-byte checks, we'll capture tcpdump and compare timestamps; do you have a header we can rely on to correlate requests (X-Redwood-Run-ID)?

If you can reply with those three items, we'll finalize the firewall change and confirm the Thu window.

Hi Rahul — quick answers inline:

- Source ports: tests originate from our managed runners and will use ephemeral high ports (32768–61000). We recommend allowing outbound on those ranges to the sandbox.
- Test key scope: yes — FINANCECORP-TEST-abc123 is scoped to redwood-sandbox-v2 and has no access to production models. We also have server-side rate limits enforced at 1k rps per key; your test run is well under that.
- Correlation header: we will attach X-Redwood-Run-ID with a UUID for every request during the run and include the same value in our logs. We'll share the UUID before the run and include it in the k6 headers.

We'll update the financecorp-ip-allowlist.csv to include NAT ranges if your infra needs them — Aditya, can you add the NAT ranges and push a new CSV by EOD?

Looking forward to the run on Thu. Marissa will follow up with the Zoom link and post-run survey.

Cheers,
